ctx.x: When all the greetings were over, Charles taken me to the hotel where a room had been reserved in the neighbourhood of Montmartre which I was familiar with. He left me and I was on my own. The hotel was called "la Bruyère" and was situated on the corner of a street by the same name and rue Pigalle, not far from the Hotel Eden where I had stayed when I came to Paris in 1935. After unpacking my bags, I decided to go out especially to Boudon's and the tabac at the corner of rue Fontaine to see if I could find any…

A few days later, I rehearsed with the musicians. I learned that Serge Griffin was the accountaſnt for the Edouard 7th theatre, and I also got together on the names of the musicians which was not easy for me to do. Barney, the pianist, was Bernard Peiffer. Mike, who played alto sax, was Michel de Villers. Joe, the vibe player was Geo Daly. John, the bass man was Jean Bouchety, and Rodger, the drummer, was Roger Paraboschi. But it was quite some time before I could pronounce those names correctly.

Bernard Peiffer had a very personal style, and sometimes, he could do a good imitation of Erroll Garner. But when he got excited his taste was bad and he seemed to be giving instructions on how to break a piano up in public without using an ax.
